\n\nAfter we seized the city of Algiers, causing the Bey of Algeria to go into exile, a power vacuum ensued in the city of Tlemcen, resulting in the populace requesting protection from Sultan Abd al-Rahman of Morocco. Thus, despite having been part of Algeria for centuries, the city has been under Moroccan administration since 1830. Our advisors have suggested forcing the Sultan to turn over the city to us, as it is an important port which would be of great strategic value in the conquest of Algeria's interior. When faced with our might, Morocco should readily back down and abandon the city.

\n\n$FROMCOUNTRY$ has sent us a delegation demanding the immediate withdrawal of our forces from the city of Tilimsan that we had taken control of following the collapse of the Bey of Algeria's authority in 1830. Considering we are already weakened by the Wadiya revolting against Sultan Abd al-Rahman's authority, it may be prudent to submit to the French demands, even if it means abandoning our brethren to a cruel fate.

The Greek uprisings have done what the western world, and even the Ottoman sultan have considered all but impossible. Without any foreign assistance, the Greek people have thrown out their oppressors from the seat of power in Constantinople, and have laid claim to all that was previously taken from them in centuries past. The city is once again ours, and we can recenter the eastern world once again around that of Constantinople, the city of kings!

Ever since the independence of the Rhomaion state, the local Turkish population and loyalists to the old Sultan's regime have raided the Greek countryside, wreaking havoc on the state's income and on the national economy. With a proper Rhomaion army finally put together, the Ottoman raids can be put to an end, and the perpetrators rightfully put to death.

With the Rhomaion state in power once again, one of the greatest weaknesses it unfortunately inherited from the Ottoman empire was a disloyal and rotting bureaucratic structure. With a hefty investment into a bureaucratic reform program, this can be dealt with.

\n\nThe Italian Peninsula has erupted into open war, as Sardinia takes advantage of the weakened state of the Austrian Empire to seize control over Lombardia. With the status quo upended, this poses an existential threat to Bourbon interests on the peninsula, and if left unchecked may well result in the collapse of the balance of powers. Intervention, while aiding an enemy in the Austrian Empire, may prove to the best interests of the French Kingdom in the long run.
The process of Germanization, thus far, has been rather slow and small in scale. However, with the realm centralized, it is only natural that these policies be expanded, though it will be costly.
As time wears on, the Germanization program must be further expanded so that the Austrian Empire can bring about yet more central control.

In the aftermath of the Spanish War of Succession, the crown of Naples was awarded in the peace deal to the Hapsburg monarchy. A valuable part of the realm, the Hapsburgs ruled over it over the course of the early 1700s, until losing it in the 1730s to the Bourbon dukes of Parma. With Italy placed under Austrian supervision, this unjust loss can finally be reversed, and Naples restored to its rightful place within the empire.

\n\nAs the Colombian troops marches through Quito and with Juan Jose Flores failing to stop Colombian advances, many in the newly formed state of Ecuador started to lose support in Flores and his attempt to free the south from Colombian rule, many Ecuadorian officers and civilians started to turn on Flores, demanding that peace is the only way to stop this bloodshed, Flores at the end had no choice but to resign and flee from his country, letting Ecuador with no choice but to be fully reintegrated into Gran Colombia.

\n\nExecuted by General Tomás Hererra, Alzuru's revolt is no more. Panama has returned to Colombian rule amid much jubilation. Many hope this is the last attempt of the separatist movements that has being happening in all Gran Colombia, totally avoiding the collapse once and for all.
